With further deformation, the BCC lattice undergoes compression along the y-axis and sliding along the z-axis within the middle planes, resulting in a transformation from BCC to HCP.

In the transition zone from pure elas - ticity to pure plasticity (shock front), the shear stress significantly de - creases, which is attributed to stress relaxation caused by dislocation nucleation.

When the shock wave reflects from the right interface and interacts with the incident wave, it leads to the annihilation of Shockley dislocations. The number of newly generated dislocations is smaller than the number of annihilated ones, resulting in a decrease in Shockley dislocation density [ 44 ].
Therefore, immobile dislocations (such as stair-rod and Hirth disloca - tions) may increase local stress, leading to strain hardening.

It can be seen that below 780 K, the increase in temperature promotes the transformation from the FCC phase to BCC phase, which yields greater plastic deformation [ 35 ].
Under compression along the < 110 > direction, the BCT can transform into a BCC lattice, which is a process known as the Bain path [ 37 ].
With further deformation, the BCC lattice undergoes compression along the y-axis and sliding along the z-axis within the middle planes, resulting in a transformation from BCC to HCP.

In the transition zone from pure elas - ticity to pure plasticity (shock front), the shear stress significantly de - creases, which is attributed to stress relaxation caused by dislocation nucleation.

When the shock wave reflects from the right interface and interacts with the incident wave, it leads to the annihilation of Shockley dislocations. The number of newly generated dislocations is smaller than the number of annihilated ones, resulting in a decrease in Shockley dislocation density [ 44 ].
Therefore, immobile dislocations (such as stair-rod and Hirth disloca - tions) may increase local stress, leading to strain hardening.
A high content of ISF indicates a high dislocation density and the presence of SLIP, so the higher the ISF, the better the material ’ s plastic deformation ability and ductility.
